task.title: Let a project move its tasks back to a place they left
task.description:
Moving a project's tasks to another repository is one-way today. After `workbook move-tasks`, `workbook config unset tasks-remote` and `workbook config set tasks-remote origin` are refused with the `moved-for-good` reason, and no tasks remote can be pointed at any place the tasks already left. Undoing a move is a documented by-hand procedure that needs a force push. Dylan's ruling (2026-11-22): moving should never be a one-way street.

## What is needed

- A project can move its tasks to any repository it can reach, including one they moved away from earlier: back to `origin`, or back to an earlier tasks repository. The same two commands do it: `workbook config set tasks-remote ...` (or `unset` / `set tasks-remote origin` to return to origin), then `workbook move-tasks`.
- The place the tasks return to stops refusing checkouts, without a force push and without deleting a ref. The marker is a commit on that place's `refs/workbook/project`; returning adds another commit on top of it (a fast-forward) that records "tasks returned" (see Decisions).
- The place the tasks leave is marked exactly as any old place is today, naming where they went.
- Returning carries everything: edits made at the newer place since the first move reach the returned-to place, each operation once, matched by operation ID and content as `move-tasks` already does. The stale copies the returned-to place still holds from before are brought up to date, including a task that was compacted in between.
- A checkout still on any earlier generation of the settings is refused and told the current place, however many moves there have been and whatever order they went in (origin → tasks → origin → third ...). Following markers must end; a loop of markers must be impossible or detected and reported.
- `moved-for-good` goes away, along with the by-hand undo procedure in `docs/reference.md`.
- A tasks-only folder (a hosted board) on a place the tasks left is repointed by the printed command as today, including when the destination is a place it was on before.

## Decisions

1. Settled by Dylan (2026-11-22): the returning commit records "tasks returned", not an address pointing at the place itself. (The reference already says the spelling of an address cannot prove two repositories are the same.)
2. To establish while building: what a 0.6.3 build does when it meets a returned-to place. Its reader accepts the identity commit and one marker shape. It must stop rather than misread, and say why; silently treating the place as still moved, or as never moved, is not acceptable. Run a build of main from before this story against the new shape and report what it does. No release ships between that work and this (both go out together as v0.7), so no released version ever holds the one-way behavior; still no new durable format generation unless there is no other way, and if there is none, stop and ask.
3. Recommended: the tip commit of a place's `refs/workbook/project` alone says whether that place is live or left, and where to look next.

## Old copies left behind

Out of scope here. A move leaves every task ref at the old place as it was at the time of the move; removing them is the job of `workbook reset`, a separate story ("Add workbook reset to wipe a checkout's or a remote's Workbook data"). This story must make a move back work whether or not the old copies are still there.

## What was tried by hand (2026-11-22, build of main at 162eca4a, throwaway repositories)

- Deleting `.workbook/` and every ref under `refs/workbook/` and then running `workbook move-tasks`: refused, "this project's settings name no tasks remote to move to". It also deletes the checkout's own copy of the tasks.
- Deleting only origin's `refs/workbook/*` and running `workbook config unset tasks-remote`: still refused `moved-for-good`, because the checkout keeps its own copy of origin's marker under `refs/workbook/remotes/origin/project`.
- What did work: delete origin's `refs/workbook/*` (which removes the marker without a force push), restore `.workbook/config.json` to the version without `tasksRemote`, delete the checkout's `refs/workbook/remotes/origin/*`, then `workbook setup` and `workbook sync`. Origin then held both tasks including an edit made after the move, and `validate --full` was clean. It leaves the tasks repository unmarked, so a checkout still on the old settings keeps publishing there unseen. That gap is what this story closes.

## Done when

- origin → tasks → origin, and origin → tasks → third → tasks, each work with the two commands, are safe to interrupt and re-run at every step, and end with every operation present exactly once at the current place (`validate --full` clean, refs compared).
- No step force-pushes or deletes a ref on any remote.
- A checkout and a tasks-only folder on each earlier generation of settings are refused and told the current place; their unpublished edits are kept and published after `setup`.
- An edit that reaches a left place late is carried by a later `move-tasks`, as today.
- A project that never set a tasks remote behaves exactly as before, checked by the recorded-session test.
- A 0.6.3 binary meeting the new marker shape stops with a message; shown by running one.
- Integration tests with temporary local bare remotes, SHA-256 where the environment supports it, each with a revert-check.
- README, `docs/reference.md`, `docs/architecture.md` (object graph of a return), `docs/hosting.md`, `CHANGELOG.md` updated; "one-way" wording removed everywhere, including `move-tasks --help` and the `config set` output.
